summary.headline: Sugs Lloyd FY26 revenue rose about 70% to INR300 crore, PAT up 71% to INR28 crore, with INR825 crore unexecuted order book.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue reached INR300 crore versus INR176 crore in FY25, ahead of the INR270 crore guidance, with EBITDA up 69% and PAT up 71% to about INR28 crore. Management said margins were held broadly flat year-on-year, though Q4 margin was about 12% versus roughly 14% for the half year, which management attributed to a delayed MAHAGENCO order and related site disruption. Growth drivers were RDSS-funded transmission and distribution work and solar EPC, plus a INR640 crore (incl. 18% GST, about INR540 crore ex-GST) SCADA order from Konkan Railway. Receivables and retention balances rose, and management flagged 40% of FY26 sales coming in Q4 as a key working-capital issue.

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: INR708 crore of the INR825 crore unexecuted order book; about 46% of FY26 revenue per analyst citation. Management expects this to be the largest contributor, with transmission billing expected from H2 FY27.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: INR110 crore of unexecuted order book; about 52% of FY26 revenue per analyst citation.

segments.name: Niche products (FPI, auto-reclosers, sectionalizers)
segments.commentary: About INR8 crore of unexecuted orders; FY26 FPI revenue about INR6.6-7 crore. Management targets about 10% of total revenue from FPIs by FY28, with margins described as far better than EPC.

guidance_outlook: Target of INR1,000 crore revenue by FY28, described as firmly on track; FY27 guided to about INR600 crore top line, described as very much achievable.
Margins expected to be maintained at about FY26 levels (EBITDA and PAT); Q1 FY27 may be somewhat lower.
Of the INR640 crore order, management expects INR200-250 crore billing in FY27, with the balance in FY28.
Management expects at least one more large SCADA-type project in FY27; project timelines 18-24 months, majority of current order book to close in about 18 months.
Compact FPI launch by Q2 FY27; VCB (switchgear) likely next year; RMUs further out pending CPRI and ERDA type testing.
Arrangements for credit limits of INR300-350 crore (fund and non-fund) to support INR1,000 crore revenue; no fundraise planned currently.
capex_capacity: Compact next-generation FPI almost ready; launch targeted by Q2 FY27.
Switchgear (VCB) at advanced stage; RMU development uses dry compressed air insulated technology; about 10 engineers on R&D, number rising.

Working on SCADA-compatible grids, ADMS, DMS and distributed automation projects; bidding on about INR1,225 crore of tenders at various stages, with about 3,000 tenders identified for bid preparation.
No specific capacity or capex figures were given in the call.
demand_pricing: Order inflow: about INR500 crore plus booked in FY26; INR639-640 crore Konkan Railway SCADA order received 17 March 2026 (about INR540 crore ex-GST); BSES order of about INR86 crore mentioned.
Management said order inflow slowed in the last three months apart from the Konkan Railway order; several pipeline orders pending accept or decline decision.
Tender strike rate estimated at 20-30%, implying 200-300 of the INR1,225 crore tenders could be won.
Payment terms on RDSS project: 60% on material supply, 30% on installation and commissioning, 10% retention released after completion against bank guarantee.
Most orders carry price variation clauses covering commodity (including LME-linked copper) and statutory tax changes.

Competitors named for large SCADA projects: L&T, Voltas and other EPC players. Management said 99% of business is with government entities, and it is bidding only on centrally or multilaterally funded projects.
Geographic expansion: Odisha and Bihar were earlier core markets; now Gujarat, Maharashtra, Punjab, Chhattisgarh; international expansion planned but not immediate.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 'other current assets' jump to INR42 crore, and is it retention money?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is retention money not yet due, released after the company discharges project obligations.

qa_highlights.question: How will receivables be managed, and what are the terms, working capital and margins on the large INR600 crore order?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40% of sales fall in Q4, with 10% carried from prior periods. Steps include a collection task force, shifting to projects with easier payment terms, and capping retention at 10%. The large order is expected to carry no margin pressure, under RDSS payment terms.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins be maintained on the new project pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins broadly similar, with quarterly variation from product and customer mix; FY26 margin levels expected to hold.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 margin fall to about 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a MAHAGENCO order delayed by a Q3 land dispute and local political interference, which raised costs; year-on-year margins described as stagnant.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FPI order book, FPI revenue, and FY28 contribution target?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR8 crore of FPI orders to be billed by June or July 2026; FY26 FPI revenue about INR7 crore. Target about 10% of revenue from FPI by FY28, possibly higher.

qa_highlights.question: What credit lines and rating does the company have, and will it need funds?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 bank facility INR125 crore; for INR1,000 crore revenue, arrangements for INR300-350 crore limits planned. No market fundraise envisaged currently; rating BBB minus (CARE).

qa_highlights.question: Execution timeline of current order book and implied revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical project timeline 18-24 months; majority of INR825 crore book expected to close in about 18 months. Management said FY27 revenue will exceed the analyst's roughly INR480 crore estimate.

risks_watch: Receivables and retention build-up; heavy Q4 concentration (40% of sales) and creditor days now at 61.
Order inflow slowdown in the last three months before the Konkan Railway win; management said pipeline decisions pending.
Dependence on government and DISCOM payments; management said it only bids on centrally or multilaterally funded projects.
Q4 margin dip (about 12%) and execution delays from political interference; Q1 FY27 margin may be lower.
Dependence on government testing approvals (CPRI, ERDA) for switchgear, VCB and RMU launches; timelines not firm.
Working-capital needs for growth to INR1,000 crore; reliance on new limits of INR300-350 crore and financing tools like TReDS and surety bonds.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, order book and FY28 target, with specific figures. Cautious and somewhat evasive on receivables, Q4 margin dip and timing of large orders, which management said are beyond its control.
key_quotes: We have been able to retain both our EBITDA margin as well as the PAT margin over this period as compared to the last year.
Our target of INR1,000 crores revenue by financial year '28 is firmly on track.
Improving receivables is our top priority and we are working hard on it.
Yes, it is very much achievable. We are on line.
